briefings.title: Beyond Bigger Models: Recursion As The Next Scaling Law In AI
briefings.tldr: Recursive AI models like Hierarchical Reasoning Models (HRM) and Tiny Recursive Models (TRM) achieve state-of-the-art reasoning performance—outperforming models 1,000x their size on tasks like the ARC Prize—by utilizing weight reuse and latent memory states at inference time to bypass the "reasoning ceiling" of standard feed-forward LLMs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Recursive AI models like Hierarchical Reasoning Models (HRM) and Tiny Recursive Models (TRM) achieve state-of-the-art reasoning performance—outperforming models 1,000x their size on tasks like the ARC Prize—by utilizing weight reuse and latent memory states at inference time to bypass the "reasoning ceiling" of standard feed-forward LLMs.

## The Structural Limits of Standard LLMs
* **Feed-Forward Constraints:** While modern LLMs excel at next-token prediction, they are essentially one-shot feed-forward processes at training time. This limits their ability to solve "incompressible" problems that require iterative computation.
* **The Sorting Analogy:** Francois Chaubard explains that a transformer with 30 layers cannot solve a comparison sort for a 31-element list because the problem has a theoretical lower bound of $N \log N$ steps. Standard models literally "run out of layers" to complete the necessary logic.
* **Discrete vs. Latent Reasoning:** 
    * **Chain of Thought (CoT):** This is a "hack" that forces recursion in the visible token space, but it is limited by human-labeled data and training traces.
    * **Recursive Latent Space:** True recursive models reason within a continuous, high-dimensional latent space (memory), making them more expressive and efficient than models that must "snap back" to discrete tokens.
* **The Einstein Test:** Standard models are bounded by the limits of human knowledge. They can use tools (like a Python sort function) because they have seen them before, but they struggle to discover new algorithms (e.g., discovering Merge Sort if they only knew Bubble Sort).

## Hierarchical Reasoning Models (HRM)
* **Architecture:** Inspired by the human brain's varying processing frequencies, HRM uses three nested levels of recursion:
    * **Low-level (L-net):** Operates at high frequency for local features.
    * **High-level (H-net):** Operates at a lower frequency for broader context.
    * **Outer Refinement Loop:** Scales the reasoning depth at inference time.
* **The "Stop Grad" Innovation:** To avoid the "vanishing gradient" problem common in old Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), HRM uses a fixed-point iteration method. 
    * **Memory Persistence:** The model performs 16 iterations but only backpropagates through a small portion, essentially treating different memory states as a "mini-batch" rather than resetting activations to zero.
* **Performance:** With only 27 million parameters and no pre-training, HRM achieved ~70% on the ARC Prize, while massive models like o3 initially scored zero.

## Tiny Recursive Models (TRM): Complexity through Simplification
* **Model Efficiency:** TRM refines the HRM approach by collapsing the dual networks into a single shared-weight transformer layer. Despite having only 7 million parameters, it outperforms HRM.
* **Architectural Shifts:**
    * **Weight Sharing:** TRM uses the same network for both high and low-level features, proving that variable scoping (distinct memory states) is more important than having distinct physical layers.
    * **Deep Supervision:** It utilizes "truncated backprop through time," backpropagating through one full recursive loop rather than a single step, which significantly boosts performance.
* **Task Specificity:** While small, these models are currently task-specific. A TRM trained for Sudoku cannot inherently solve ARC puzzles, marking a departure from the general-purpose nature of LLMs.

## The Future of Scaling: Depth over Width
* **Compute Depth:** The "next scaling law" involves increasing compute depth (recursion steps) rather than just parameter width. 
* **Merging Paradigms:** The ultimate frontier in AI research is combining the representation power of giant foundation models (like Gemini or GPT-4) with the recursive reasoning engines of TRMs.
* **Latent Reasoning:** Future architectures will likely move reasoning into the latent "embedding" space rather than relying on the inefficient, token-by-token Chain of Thought method.

## Notable Quotes

> "It is actually impossible for the [standard LLM] model to map from an unsorted list to a sorted list on a one-shot basis... if I have a list that's 31 elements long and my transformer is 30 [layers], I run out of steps to do comparisons." — **Francois Chaubard**

> "This is why this paper is so exciting: [TRM] is a 7-million parameter model that can solve what a trillion-parameter model can't solve, even when the latter is trained on the entire internet." — **Francois Chaubard**

> "In the case of RNNs in general, they remain in this continuous latent space which is much, much higher dimensional... It’s much more expressive to be in continuous space, but we couldn't train it that way because you're inhibited by backprop through time." — **Ankit Gupta**

> "We found mapping from pixels to some really cool latent space where things are nicely semantically separated... But now in that space, use these tiny reasoning models—use some type of recursion inside that—and I think that’s going to really work." — **Francois Chaubard**

briefings.title: Can America trust AI? David Sacks makes the case.
briefings.tldr: David Sacks, special advisor to President Trump on AI, argues for a "let them cook" regulatory philosophy of permissionless innovation to ensure American dominance in a global race against China, emphasizing that AI will ultimately solve the very problems it creates.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
David Sacks, special advisor to President Trump on AI, argues for a "let them cook" regulatory philosophy of permissionless innovation to ensure American dominance in a global race against China, emphasizing that AI will ultimately solve the very problems it creates.

## The Trump Administration’s "Permissionless Innovation" Framework
* **Global Competition:** Sacks views AI as an "infinite game" where the U.S. cannot afford to slow down; unilateral disarmament would simply cede leadership to China, where half of the world’s AI developers are located.
* **The Three Pillars of AI Policy:**
    * **Pro-Innovation:** Adopting a "let them cook" philosophy that favors private sector leadership with minimally burdensome federal regulation.
    * **Pro-Infrastructure:** Aligning AI needs with "drill, baby, drill" energy policies to meet the massive power demands of data centers.
    * **Pro-Export:** Ensuring American chips and models maintain global market share to preserve U.S. "soft power."
* **Preempting State Regulation:** The White House framework aims to provide a national alternative to the 1,200+ bills currently moving through state legislatures, which Sacks characterizes as "knee-jerk regulation."

## Targeted Regulation and Public Safety
* **Parental Empowerment:** Regarding online child safety and AI chatbots, Sacks argues the "North Star" should be giving parents the tools to decide app usage and screen time rather than government bans.
* **Ratepayer Protection:** To combat local opposition to data centers (NIMBYism), the administration secured a pledge from major AI companies to ensure new data centers do not increase residential electricity prices.
    * **The "Quid Pro Quo":** AI companies are encouraged to become "power companies," bringing their own energy sources in exchange for streamlined building permits.
* **Liability Standards:** Sacks opposes holding AI developers liable for the actions of end-users, comparing it to holding Microsoft Excel responsible for a money launderer’s spreadsheets. He supports "red teaming" to prevent models from providing instructions for bioweapons or nuclear devices.

## National Security and the "AI Equilibrium"
* **The Pentagon Chain of Command:** Sacks criticizes AI companies (specifically citing the Anthropic dispute) that attempt to veto the "lawful uses" of their products by the military. He argues that companies selling to the Department of Defense must respect the established chain of command.
* **Cybersecurity Arms Race:** Regarding "Mythos," a potent hacking tool held back from public release, Sacks believes the market will reach a new equilibrium.
    * **Defensive Parity:** He argues that AI's ability to find coding vulnerabilities will be used by "white hats" to patch systems before "black hats" can exploit them.
* **Orwellian vs. Terminator Risks:** Sacks is less concerned about "The Terminator" and more concerned with an "Orwellian" future where government and corporate power merge to surveil and censor citizens.

## Economic Outlook and the "Pessimism Gap"
* **Debunking Job Loss Narratives:** Sacks claims there is "no discernible disruption" to the labor market yet, citing that less than 5% of recent layoffs are attributable to AI. 
    * **The Construction Boom:** He highlights a massive $650 billion investment in CAPEX, which has led to a 25-30% wage increase for blue-collar workers (electricians, plumbers, and drywallers) building AI infrastructure.
* **White-Collar Transformation:** While acknowledging shifts in coding and research, Sacks views AI as a "productivity explosion" and a leveler for young workers, rather than a tool for total job evaporation.
* **The Optimism Deficit:** Sacks identifies public fear as the biggest threat to U.S. leadership. He notes that while 83% of Chinese citizens are "AI-optimistic," only 39% of Americans share that view.

> AI is going to solve the problem that AI creates. That's kind of my view on where that market is going.
— **David Sacks**

> If in five years we look around the world and all the data centers are running on Huawei chips and DeepSeek models, that means that we lost. We don't want to have that future.
— **David Sacks**

> I just don't think it was a very realistic position for them [Anthropic] to take to say that they can dictate to a government agency what lawful uses of their product should be allowed.
— **David Sacks**

briefings.title: Earnings Keep the Market Strong Despite Signs of Consumer Weakness | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: The U.S. economy remains bifurcated ("K-shaped"), where massive AI-driven infrastructure spending by Big Tech and industrials continues to propel the market upward despite clear evidence of a recession among low-to-middle-income consumers.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The U.S. economy remains bifurcated ("K-shaped"), where massive AI-driven infrastructure spending by Big Tech and industrials continues to propel the market upward despite clear evidence of a recession among low-to-middle-income consumers.

## The AI Arms Race and Industrial Beneficiaries
The primary driver of current GDP and market strength is the unabated surge in Capital Expenditure (CapEx) related to artificial intelligence.

*   **Big Tech Earnings:** Results from Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta confirm no slowdown in AI spending.
    *   **Google:** Significant acceleration in cloud revenue ($20B) drove a 10% stock surge.
    *   **Microsoft:** Azure grew 39%, though the stock softened as investors sought even higher beats.
    *   **Amazon:** AWS revenue rose 28%, and the company reported $225B in revenue commitments for its "Trainium" AI chip.
    *   **Meta:** Despite beating metrics, shares fell after the company raised its 2026 CapEx outlook to $135B, signaling a high-cost battle for AI dominance.
*   **Industrial Infrastructure:** The "data center boom" is fueling non-tech sectors.
    *   **Quanta Services:** Benefiting from utility construction and maintenance required for AI power needs.
    *   **Caterpillar:** Sales grew 38% in the construction unit, driven largely by data center equipment demand.

## The K-Shaped Economy: Consumer Divergence
Earnings reports reveal a sharp divide between the financial health of different consumer segments.

*   **Signs of Weakness:**
    *   **Domino’s Pizza:** Weak same-store sales (0.9% vs. 2.3% expected) suggest the low-to-middle-end consumer is currently in a "deep recession."
    *   **Starbucks:** Despite a difficult backdrop, reported its second straight quarter of traffic growth, suggesting business changes are finally taking hold.
*   **Signs of Strength:**
    *   **Visa:** Net revenue rose 17% with payment volumes up 9%, indicating that overall consumer spending remains robust at the higher end of the "K."
    *   **Eli Lilly:** Reported a "blowout" quarter (EPS of $8.55 vs. $6.66 expected), confirming its dominance in the weight-loss drug market.

## High-Conviction Plays and Market Risks
Steve Eisman detailed his specific thesis on several controversial or high-profile names.

*   **Charter Communications (Conviction Long):** Despite a 25% stock drop following a loss of 120,000 broadband subscribers, Eisman is holding and adding to his position.
    *   **Thesis:** CapEx is scheduled to drop from $11B to ~$7.5B by 2028, which should theoretically drive massive free cash flow for stock buybacks.
*   **FICO (Conviction Short):** Eisman remains short, citing a massive pricing disparity between FICO and its competitor, VantageScore.
    *   **The Math:** For every 100 applications, FICO charges ~$2,049 compared to VantageScore’s ~$99. Eisman believes lenders will inevitably shift toward the lower-cost provider once implementation begins in 2027.
*   **Private Credit Concerns:** Eisman questioned the "marks" on software loans within private credit portfolios (specifically Ares and Blue Owl).
    *   **Refinancing Risk:** With public software valuations down significantly (ServiceNow used as a proxy), many private equity-backed software firms may find it impossible to refinance loans when their equity value has halved.

## Geopolitics and Macro Trends
Global alliances and market concentrations are shifting, creating new layers of uncertainty.

*   **The UAE’s Exit from OPEC:** A "canary moment" signaling a shift in worldwide alliances. The UAE appears ready to "go it alone" to increase production and grab market share amid the Iran conflict.
*   **Energy Prices:** Brent crude has climbed above $115 as the U.S. maintains a blockage of the Strait of Hormuz to pressure Iran economically.
*   **Market Concentration:** Semiconductors now constitute 16% of the S&P 500. This makes the entire index hypersensitive to any negative news regarding AI or data center demand.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "When a pizza company shows weak same-store sales, it implies that the middle and low-end consumer is having a hard time... the bottom of the K consumers are in a deep recession." — **Steve Eisman**

> "There is no slowdown in AI CapEx on the horizon. AI CapEx is what is driving GDP, and a strong GDP drives the stock market." — **Steve Eisman**

> "Regime changes are notoriously difficult to predict. [Commentators] argued that stagflation had arrived... and yet, on this rally, the leaders were the same leaders of the last few years: tech stocks and banks." — **Steve Eisman**

briefings.title: Jensen Huang & Anirudh Devgan on Design for AI and AI for Design at CadenceLIVE 2026 – Fireside Chat
briefings.tldr: The industry is shifting from generative AI that "knows" to agentic AI that "does," effectively expanding the chip design workforce by 1,000x as virtual agents use specialized EDA tools to solve complex optimization and physical design problems.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The industry is shifting from generative AI that "knows" to agentic AI that "does," effectively expanding the chip design workforce by 1,000x as virtual agents use specialized EDA tools to solve complex optimization and physical design problems.

## The Shift from Generative to Agentic AI
* **The "Knowing" vs. "Doing" Inflection Point:** Jensen Huang emphasized that while generative AI (perception and knowledge) was the first step, the current "agentic" revolution allows AI to reason, execute plans, and use external tools.
* **The "Microwave" Analogy for Tool Use:** Huang argued that agents will not reinvent fundamental engineering algorithms but will instead use them as tools. 
    * Just as a household robot would use a microwave rather than emitting radiation from its fingers, AI agents will use Cadence’s established EDA tools to verify and refine designs.
* **Scaling Beyond Human Constraints:** Historically, the semiconductor industry has been limited by the number of human designers ("butts in seats"). In the agentic era, growth is limited only by compute and token budgets.

## AI-Driven Specialized Chip Design Agents
* **Domain-Specific Agents:** NVIDIA and Cadence are collaborating on several specialized agents to handle the most labor-intensive parts of chip design:
    * **ChipStack:** Focuses on RTL (Register Transfer Level) and verification, specializing in complex protocols like PCIe Express and CXL.
    * **VeraStack:** An agent for analog design, which has traditionally been difficult to automate due to the extreme limits of physics and signal integrity.
* **Physical Design Optimization:** Physical design is described as a "many-variable, impossible-to-find-a-perfect-answer" search algorithm. 
    * Agents allow for massive parallelization, running thousands of permutations 24/7 to find the best PPA (Power, Performance, Area) solutions.
* **Virtual Engineers:** Anirudh Devgan noted that virtual agents are already integrated into NVIDIA’s workflows, participating in Slack channels alongside human engineers to solve specific design bugs.

## The Rise of Physical AI and Robotics
* **The "ChatGPT Moment" for Robotics:** The industry has arrived at the Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model era. This allows for "pixels-in, action-out" capabilities, enabling robots to understand physicality and reason through complex scenarios.
* **Synthetic Data and World Models:** Because physical data is harder to gather than text, NVIDIA and Cadence are using "AI Physics" to generate synthetic data.
    * **High-Fidelity Simulation:** Cadence’s acquisition of MSC (Adams) provides the high-fidelity physics solvers needed to train NVIDIA’s Cosmos and Isaac platforms.
    * **Reasoning in Motion:** Huang highlighted "Alpha Mo," a reasoning car that can "think out loud" to navigate complex environments (e.g., deciding to move around a truck parked in its lane).

## Post-Agentic Leadership and Business Strategy
* **The Token Budget Paradigm:** Huang predicts that future engineering productivity will be measured by token usage. 
    * If a team isn't spending hundreds of millions—or even billions—of tokens on agents, they are likely failing to maximize their scope of responsibility.
* **The "Full-Stack" Company:** Devgan and Huang agreed that engineering is no longer siloed. Designing a modern chip requires a full-stack understanding of the software, the systems, and even the "AI factories" (data centers) where they reside.
* **Expanded TAM for EDA:** By moving from chips into physical systems (robotics, automotive, CFD), Cadence is expanding its Total Addressable Market (TAM) to include every industry that designs physical products.

> "People who are 'know-it-alls' are interesting but not valuable. People who can do things are valuable. AI went from knowing everything... to now being able to use tools." — **Jensen Huang**

> "The number of ASIC designers is likely to increase by a thousand times in the near future... In the future, we’re only limited by compute." — **Jensen Huang**

> "One thing remarkable about chip design is how much effort we put in verification... it takes one person to design it, and 100 engineers to fix it. [With agents], my Slack channel will be 99% Cadence." — **Anirudh Devgan**

> "If a company isn't spending billions of dollars of tokens a year, obviously we’re not going to be producing the things that we’re doing. These are new sensibilities that are coming in." — **Jensen Huang**

briefings.title: OpenAI Misses Targets, Codex vs Claude, Elon vs Sam Trial, Big Hyperscaler Beats, Peptide Craze
briefings.tldr: Big Tech is undergoing a massive structural shift toward an asset-heavy "industrial" model, with CAPEX projections hitting $1 trillion as companies scramble for power and compute, while OpenAI faces internal friction over missed growth targets despite maintaining a product edge over a compute-constrained Anthropic.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Big Tech is undergoing a massive structural shift toward an asset-heavy "industrial" model, with CAPEX projections hitting $1 trillion as companies scramble for power and compute, while OpenAI faces internal friction over missed growth targets despite maintaining a product edge over a compute-constrained Anthropic.

## OpenAI Performance and the Compute Choke Point
*   **Missed Milestones:** OpenAI reportedly missed its 2025 revenue targets and its goal of reaching one billion weekly active users (WAUs). Internal tensions have surfaced between CEO Sam Altman and CFO Sarah Friar regarding IPO readiness and massive spending commitments.
*   **The "Contrarian" Product View:** David Sacks argues that despite the bad press, OpenAI is winning the product war. GPT 5.5 (based on the "Spud" model) is gaining developer momentum while Anthropic’s Opus 4.7 is reportedly being "rationed" and compute-gated due to capacity constraints.
*   **Power as the Choke Point:** Chamath Palihapitiya identifies electricity, not just chips, as the ultimate bottleneck.
    *   **Grid Infrastructure:** Less than half of announced power projects are actually being built due to red tape and supply chain delays for transformers and turbines.
    *   **Hyperscaler Advantage:** The shortage benefits "hyperscalers" (Oracle, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Google) who control the power, forcing smaller labs to trade equity for compute access.
*   **Algorithmic Efficiency:** David Friedberg highlighted new MIT research on "pruning" techniques that could reduce model size by 90% with no loss in accuracy, potentially offering a 10x improvement in inference per energy unit.

## The $1 Trillion CAPEX Explosion
*   **Massive Infrastructure Spend:** Four major companies (Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Meta) have signaled ~$725 billion in CAPEX guidance through 2026. Including smaller players, total AI infrastructure build-out is approaching $1 trillion.
*   **Cloud Growth Numbers:** 
    *   **Google Cloud:** Grew 63% YoY on $20B revenue.
    *   **Microsoft Cloud:** Grew 30% on $34.7B revenue.
    *   **AWS:** Grew 28% on $37.6B revenue.
*   **Cash Flow Erosion:** The era of "asset-light" software is ending. Amazon’s free cash flow dropped 97% as it pivots to physical infrastructure. Chamath suggests these companies will eventually resemble "bulky industrial businesses" with high leverage and complex financial engineering.
*   **AI as GDP Engine:** Sacks noted that AI infrastructure was responsible for a significant portion of recent U.S. GDP growth, arguing that "AI is now synonymous with the growth of the American economy."

## Legal and Regulatory Developments
*   **Elon Musk vs. Sam Altman:** The trial regarding OpenAI’s transition to a for-profit entity has entered discovery.
    *   **The "Smoking Gun":** Evidence includes a diary kept by Greg Brockman documenting plans to transition to a for-profit model while potentially misleading Musk.
    *   **Charitable Trust:** Musk's legal team is arguing "breach of charitable trust," claiming a non-profit cannot be "looted" for private gain.
*   **Supreme Court (Friedberg’s Dispatch):** David Friedberg attended oral arguments for the Bayer/Monsanto Roundup case.
    *   **Federal Preemption:** The core issue is whether the EPA’s federal labeling (which says Roundup does not cause cancer) preempts state laws (like California’s "failure to warn" laws).
    *   **Chevron Doctrine Impact:** The recent overturning of the Chevron Doctrine complicates the case, as states now argue they shouldn't have to defer blindly to federal agencies.

## AI Frontiers: Cybersecurity, "Vibecoding," and Peptides
*   **The Cyber Upgrade Cycle:** OpenAI released GPT 5.5 Cyber to compete with Anthropic’s "Mithos." Sacks argues this will create a massive one-time upgrade cycle as AI "white hats" find and patch dormant bugs before "black hats" can exploit them.
*   **The "Vibecoding" Disaster:** An autonomous AI agent (vibe-coding) recently deleted a production database and its backups in nine seconds due to a credential mismatch.
    *   **The Lesson:** AI currently lacks "low confidence" triggers—it doesn't know when to stop and ask for human permission before performing destructive acts.
*   **Retatrutide (The "Triple Agonist"):** A new peptide from Eli Lilly is showing revolutionary results in Phase 3 trials.
    *   **Metabolic Impact:** By binding to three receptors (GLP-1, GIP, and Glucagon), it reportedly reduces liver fat by 80% and favors fat burning over muscle loss.
    *   **Timeline:** FDA approval is projected for mid-2027, though high demand is already driving "peptide craze" discussions in fitness and longevity communities.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "Everything in this market is power-constrained. The reason that these folks may miss a number or a forecast has nothing to do with demand. It is entirely, 100 percent due to the supply of the power necessary to generate the output token." — **Chamath Palihapitiya**

> "If we make it okay to loot a charity, the entire foundation of charitable giving in America will be destroyed. That's my concern." — **Elon Musk (quoted regarding OpenAI lawsuit)**

> "AI is now synonymous with the growth of the American economy. When you talk about stopping AI or halting progress, you're basically saying you don't want economic growth." — **David Sacks**

> "It’s possible that [the AI] decided that the most efficient way to get rid of all the bugs was to get rid of all the software, which is technically and statistically correct." — **Jason Calacanis (joking on the 'Vibecoding' disaster)**

briefings.title: Qualcomm Q2 FY26 earnings call
briefings.tldr: Qualcomm delivered solid Q2 results with record automotive growth and is pivoting toward "agentic AI" as its primary growth engine, despite temporary handset headwinds caused by memory industry dynamics.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Qualcomm delivered solid Q2 results with record automotive growth and is pivoting toward "agentic AI" as its primary growth engine, despite temporary handset headwinds caused by memory industry dynamics. The company announced its first major custom silicon win with a leading hyperscaler, signaling a significant expansion into the data center market.

## Financial Performance & Handset Market Dynamics
* **Q2 Results:** Qualcomm reported revenues of $10.6 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $2.65, hitting the high end of guidance.
    * **QCT Revenue:** $9.1 billion, driven by record automotive and IoT growth.
    * **QTL (Licensing) Revenue:** $1.4 billion with a 72% EBT margin.
* **Handset Recovery Outlook:** While QCT handset revenues ($6 billion) were impacted by OEMs drawing down inventory due to high memory costs, management expects a recovery soon.
    * **China Bottoming:** China Android revenue is expected to bottom out in fiscal Q3 and return to sequential growth in Q4.
    * **Apple Partnership:** Qualcomm maintains a 20% share assumption for the 2026 iPhone launch, with roughly $2 billion in product revenue modeled for fiscal 2027.
* **Capital Return:** The company returned $3.7 billion to stockholders during the quarter, including $2.8 billion in share repurchases.

## The Paradigm Shift: Agentic AI & PC Leadership
* **The "Agentic" Opportunity:** CEO Cristiano Amon highlighted that "agentic AI" (AI agents running continuously in the background) is fundamentally reshaping the product roadmap.
    * **CPU Focus:** Unlike early AI which was GPU-heavy, agent orchestration is predominantly CPU-bound, playing to the strengths of Qualcomm’s Oryon CPU.
    * **Upgrade Cycle:** Management believes current devices are not built for background agents, creating a massive multi-year upgrade opportunity across smartphones and PCs.
* **Snapdragon X2 PC Platform:** Now in production, the X2 platform is positioned as a market leader.
    * **Performance Lead:** The platform reportedly outperforms Intel’s Panther Lake by nearly 30% in end-to-end agentic experiences.
    * **Industry Reception:** Management cited third-party reviews stating Qualcomm is no longer just catching up but is now "setting the pace" in the PC space.

## Automotive & Industrial Growth
* **Record Automotive Revenue:** The segment reached a $5 billion annualized revenue run rate for the first time, with a target to exceed $6 billion by the end of fiscal 2026.
    * **Content Increase:** The upcoming 5th Gen Snapdragon Digital Chassis represents the largest content increase in company history, featuring 12x NPU performance for Level 3 and Level 4 autonomous driving.
    * **ADAS Adoption:** Over 1 million cars are now operating ADAS and autonomy on Snapdragon Ride processors, with significant traction from BMW, Bosch, and Vay.
* **Industrial & Physical AI:**
    * **DragonWing IQ10:** A new platform for industrial robotics featuring 700 TOPS of AI performance and support for over 20 camera sensors.
    * **Robotics Partnerships:** Building on its win with Figure AI, Qualcomm announced a new multi-year agreement with Neura.

## Strategic Diversification: Data Center & 6G
* **Data Center Custom Silicon:** Qualcomm has entered the custom silicon space for a "large hyperscaler," with initial shipments expected in the December quarter. 
    * **AlphaWave Integration:** The integration of AlphaWave is accelerating execution in the custom ASIC market.
* **6G Strategy:** Qualcomm is positioning itself as the architect of 6G, which it defines as an "AI-native" network.
    * **Timeline:** Prototype demonstrations are expected in 2028, with commercial scale-up by 2030.
    * **Use Cases:** Beyond connectivity, 6G will support "wide area real-time sensing" for digital twins, drone tracking, and autonomous traffic management.

> "We are in a period of profound change... Agent orchestration is predominantly CPU bound, and Qualcomm has the world's best-performing CPU across smartphones, PCs, auto, and soon the data center." 
> — **Cristiano Amon, President & CEO**

> "Our China QCT Android shipments are meaningfully below the scale of end consumer handset demand... we feel confident that the third quarter is now the bottom." 
> — **Akash Palkhiwala, CFO & COO**

> "The generational leap from the original Snapdragon X Elite to the X2 series is particularly striking. Qualcomm hasn’t just caught up to the industry, in some cases it’s now helping to set the pace." 
> — **Cristiano Amon (quoting PC Mag)**

briefings.title: Reid Hoffman On The Case For AI Optimism
briefings.tldr: Reid Hoffman argues that AI represents a "Cognitive Industrial Revolution" where success is measured by technological frontier-building rather than short-term financials; while labor displacement in scripted roles is inevitable, the focus must shift to using AI to democratize essential services like healthcare and education.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Reid Hoffman argues that AI represents a "Cognitive Industrial Revolution" where success is measured by technological frontier-building rather than short-term financials; while labor displacement in scripted roles is inevitable, the focus must shift to using AI to democratize essential services like healthcare and education.

## The State of OpenAI and the Path to IPO
* **Investment Philosophy:** Hoffman, an early investor in OpenAI and a Microsoft board member, dismissed concerns regarding OpenAI missing revenue and user targets.
    * **Prioritizing Frontier Models:** He argues that the quality of technology (e.g., the 5.5 release) is the leading indicator for future growth, regardless of current quarter-over-quarter reliability.
    * **Public Market Scrutiny:** Hoffman compares AI companies to early Amazon or Tesla—entities that trade on a "foundational promise" of the future rather than traditional P/E ratios.
* **Unit Economics:** The industry is currently in a race to an "asymptote" where the exponential cost of training models eventually meets the physical limits of power (gigawatts) and capital.
    * **Inference vs. Training:** While training costs are skyrocketing, the economics for "inference" (running the models for users) are already becoming viable and attractive.

## The Global Competitive Landscape
* **Tiered Rankings:** Hoffman identifies a distinct hierarchy among the major players:
    * **Tier 1 (The Leaders):** OpenAI and Anthropic currently hold the strongest positions in terms of frontier capabilities.
    * **Tier 2 (Big Tech):** Google (Gemini) is the primary challenger, followed by Meta and Microsoft’s internal efforts.
    * **The "Glengarry Glen Ross" Market:** In specialized fields like coding, Hoffman notes a "winner-takes-most" dynamic. Currently, Claude Code (Anthropic) leads in interaction, while OpenAI Codex leads in long-form reasoning.
* **The China Factor:** Chinese models like ByteDance’s multimodal video tools and the Qwen open-source model are highly credible but often rely on "distillation" (learning from Western frontier models). Hoffman believes future distillation will become significantly harder.
* **Apple's Lag:** Hoffman noted that Apple appears behind the curve, remarking that "they still don't seem to realize that Siri is like 20 years old in tech terms."

## AI Risks: Cybersecurity and Labor
* **Mythos and the "Crime Scene" Computer:** Hoffman addressed Anthropic's warnings about "Mythos" (their latest agentic capability).
    * **Automated Penetration Testing:** AI allows for an "infinite" number of virtual cybersecurity engineers. This fundamentally shifts the landscape by allowing rogue actors to probe billions of lines of legacy code that were previously too expensive to attack.
* **The Cognitive Industrial Revolution:** Hoffman admits the transition will be painful, specifically for "scripted" labor.
    * **High-Risk Sectors:** Customer service jobs are expected to "go completely away," and sales roles will undergo massive structural shifts.
    * **Historical Parallel:** Much like the Industrial Revolution eliminated "horse-cleanup jobs" but created the automotive industry, AI will create new, currently unpredictable roles.
    * **Transition Strategy:** Hoffman advocates for deploying AI *for* the transition—using it to help displaced workers find new roles and acquire new skills.

## Social Responsibility and the "80% Solution"
* **Democratizing Expertise:** Hoffman suggests that governments should negotiate deals with AI labs to provide "free-at-point-of-use" AI assistants on every smartphone.
    * **Essential Services:** These would include a medical assistant, a legal assistant, and a tutor for every citizen to offset the economic "melee" of the transition.
* **Wealth Inequality vs. Prosperity:** Hoffman is less concerned with "inequality" as a metric and more focused on whether the "bulk of 80% of society" sees their circumstances improve.
    * **Progressive Taxation:** While he supports progressive taxation to fix social dysfunctions, he argues it is not a sufficient solution on its own without fundamental economic renovation.

## Legal Battles and Market Speculation
* **Elon Musk vs. OpenAI:** Hoffman characterized Musk’s lawsuit against OpenAI as "legal harassment" and "factually incorrect." He claims Musk attempted to take 80% ownership of the company and left when the board refused, only to sue later when the organization succeeded.
* **SpaceX IPO Rumors:** Hoffman expressed skepticism regarding a potential SpaceX IPO, suggesting that some investors may be buying in based on "Bitcoin-style" momentum rather than sane investing behavior. He noted rumors that Musk might eventually attempt to merge SpaceX with Tesla to bolster market cap.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "I tend to think a little bit on the coding side... it’s a Glengarry Glen Ross market: first prize Cadillac, second prize steak knives, third prize you're fired." — **Reid Hoffman**

> "One of the things that's been a bit of a social problem over the last few decades has been that so much of the growth has been contained only to the private markets... I think that's one of the benefits of having some of these AI companies go public." — **Reid Hoffman**

> "The Industrial Age was really painful in terms of its transition... I think the same thing is true of the Cognitive Industrial Revolution with AI, but the transition is really painful. How do we make the transition better? The simplest thing is: deploy AI for it." — **Reid Hoffman**

briefings.title: Trump on dissatisfaction with Iran, potential Spirit bailout, King Charles: Full press conference
briefings.tldr: President Trump expressed dissatisfaction with current negotiation terms with a "disjointed" Iranian leadership, while emphasizing a "USA First" economic agenda characterized by aggressive EU auto tariffs, record domestic job growth, and potential federal intervention to save 14,000 jobs at Spirit.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump expressed dissatisfaction with current negotiation terms with a "disjointed" Iranian leadership, while emphasizing a "USA First" economic agenda characterized by aggressive EU auto tariffs, record domestic job growth, and potential federal intervention to save 14,000 jobs at Spirit.

## Iran and Middle East Security
* **Negotiation Status:** Iran reportedly seeks a deal due to a decimated military, but the President remains "not satisfied" with current terms.
    * **Disjointed Leadership:** The President characterized Iranian leadership as divided into three or four argumentative groups, making cohesive negotiation difficult.
    * **Military Capability:** Trump asserted that Iran’s navy, air force, and radar capabilities have been "wiped out" and its military "defeated."
* **Nuclear Non-Proliferation:** A primary red line remains the prevention of Iran acquiring a nuclear weapon, which the President stated would cause "problems the likes of which the world has never seen."
* **Strategic Blockade:** The Strait is described as "100 percent shut down" via a "flawless" blockade, which has trapped record amounts of oil in tankers.
* **Regional Support:** Trump expressed strong support for the new head of Iraq and maintained "tremendous respect" for the leadership in Pakistan.

## Trade and Domestic Manufacturing
* **EU Auto Tariffs:** Tariffs on cars and trucks from the European Union were raised to 25% because the EU was "not adhering" to existing trade agreements.
    * **Impact:** The administration claims these tariffs force foreign manufacturers to move production to the U.S. more quickly.
* **Manufacturing Boom:** Over $100 billion in new car plants are currently under construction in the U.S. by companies from Japan, South Korea, Canada, and Mexico.
* **China Relations:** The President previewed an upcoming "amazing" trip to China to meet with Chairman Xi, noting that negotiations are ongoing.

## Economic Policy and Corporate Assistance
* **Corporate Bailouts:** The administration is evaluating a deal to help **Spirit** (Spirit AeroSystems) to save 14,000 jobs, though Trump emphasized that any deal must be "America First" and provide a return to the U.S.
    * **Intel Precedent:** Trump cited a previous deal with Intel that allegedly resulted in a $40 billion profit for the United States.
* **Tax Proposals:** The President highlighted several key tax initiatives intended to stimulate the economy:
    * No tax on tips or overtime pay.
    * No tax on Social Security for seniors.
    * Tax deductions for interest on loans for American-made cars.
* **Energy Prices:** While acknowledging high gasoline prices, the President predicted they would "tumble" significantly once current conflicts end and the oil currently trapped in tankers is released.

## Military Authority and Defense
* **War Powers Act:** The President dismissed the War Powers Act as "unconstitutional" and "never adhered to" by previous presidents, arguing against its use to restrict his authority.
* **Military Inventory:** Trump criticized the Biden administration for giving away military inventory to Ukraine without compensation. He claimed the U.S. military is currently "locked and loaded" with double the inventory held at the start of the current period.
* **UK Relations:** Trump spoke warmly of a "high-quality" meeting with King Charles and the Queen, praising the King’s previous work and their current relationship.

> "Iran wants to make a deal because they have no military left, essentially... but at this moment, I'm not satisfied with what they're saying." — **President Donald Trump**

> "We have a trade deal with the European Union. They were not adhering to it, so I raised the tariffs on cars and trucks to 25 percent. That's billions of dollars coming into the United States." — **President Donald Trump**

> "USA first, America first. That’s my point, including with airlines, including with Intel... we're looking at Spirit, and if we can help them we will, but we have to come first." — **President Donald Trump**

> "As soon as the war ends, gasoline prices are going to tumble because there is so much right now on the scene already loaded into tankers that can't escape the strait." — **President Donald Trump**

briefings.title: WATCH: Trump says he raised tariffs on autos from EU to 25%
briefings.tldr: President Trump announced a 25% tariff on European Union auto imports due to alleged trade deal violations and expressed skepticism toward a new Iranian proposal, citing "disjointed" leadership in Tehran.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump announced a 25% tariff on European Union auto imports due to alleged trade deal violations and expressed skepticism toward a new Iranian proposal, citing "disjointed" leadership in Tehran.

## Iran and Nuclear Security
* **Negotiation Status:** President Trump confirmed that Iran is seeking a deal, but stated he is currently unsatisfied with their proposal. 
    * **Leadership Discord:** He characterized the Iranian leadership as "all messed up" and "disjointed," split between three or four different factions that cannot agree.
* **Military Assessment:** Trump claimed the Iranian military has been effectively neutralized.
    * **Asset Loss:** He stated their navy and air force have been "wiped out" and they currently lack functional radar or anti-aircraft capabilities.
* **Criticism of European Allies:** The President expressed dissatisfaction with Italy and Spain regarding their stance on Iran.
    * **Nuclear Proliferation:** He criticized any nation that would allow Iran to possess a nuclear weapon, calling such a position "not very smart."

## Trade and Auto Tariffs
* **EU Tariff Increase:** The U.S. has raised tariffs on cars and trucks from the European Union to 25%.
    * **Justification:** Trump alleged the EU was not adhering to the existing trade agreement.
    * **Production Incentives:** The administration's goal is to force European manufacturers to move factory production to the United States.
* **Domestic Manufacturing Growth:** Trump claimed that over $100 billion is currently being spent on building new car plants within the U.S.
    * **Foreign Investment:** He noted that companies from Japan, South Korea, Canada, and Mexico are among those currently expanding their U.S. manufacturing footprint.

## Diplomatic Relations: Iraq and Pakistan
* **Iraq Leadership:** Trump confirmed a phone call with the recent election winner in Iraq, whom he described as a "very good man."
    * **U.S. Support:** He claimed the victory occurred with "our help" and pledged that the United States is "with him all the way."
* **Pakistan Negotiations:** The President expressed "tremendous respect" for the Prime Minister and the Field Marshal of Pakistan.
    * **Remote Diplomacy:** Due to the length of the trip, negotiations are currently being handled "telephonically" rather than by sending an envoy to Islamabad.

## Executive Authority and Congress
* **Congressional Approval:** When questioned about seeking congressional approval for certain extensions, Trump dismissed the necessity.
    * **Constitutional Stance:** He argued that such approval has never been sought by previous administrations and claimed that many consider it "totally unconstitutional" to require it.
    * **Communication:** He maintained that while he does not seek formal approval, the administration remains "in touch" with Congress.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "Iran wants to make a deal, because they have no military left, essentially. And, they want to make a deal, but I'm not satisfied with it." — **Donald Trump**

> "We raised the tariffs because they were not, as usual, they were not adhering to the agreement that we have... it forces them to move their factory production much faster." — **Donald Trump**

> "The leadership [in Iran] is very disjointed. It's got two to three groups, maybe four... they all want to make a deal, but they're all messed up." — **Donald Trump**

> "We're always in touch with Congress, but nobody's ever sought it [approval] before, nobody's ever asked for it before... Why should we be different?" — **Donald Trump**

briefings.title: ‘Write-Downs To Zero’: The $1.8 Trillion Private Credit Warning - Danielle DiMartino Booth

people.name: Danielle DiMartino Booth
people.role: CEO and Chief Strategist, QI Research

briefings.tldr: Despite surface-level market optimism, Danielle DiMartino Booth warns of an imminent "industrial recession" and a looming liquidity crisis in the $1.8 trillion private credit market as corporate margins collapse and actual labor data reveals significant middle-class distress.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Despite surface-level market optimism, Danielle DiMartino Booth warns of an imminent "industrial recession" and a looming liquidity crisis in the $1.8 trillion private credit market as corporate margins collapse and actual labor data reveals significant middle-class distress.

## The Federal Reserve’s "Fractured" Leadership
* **Unprecedented Dissent:** The recent 8-to-4 vote on policy represents the largest committee split since 1992, signaling a loss of consensus as inflation remains sticky.
* **Transition to Kevin Warsh:** Incoming Chair Kevin Warsh (expected mid-May) inherits a "fractured" Fed. 
    * **Powell's Role:** Outgoing Chair Jay Powell has signaled he will step back into a governor role and remain deferential, avoiding becoming a "shadow chair."
    * **Alternative Data:** Warsh is expected to utilize alternative data sources—such as small business bankruptcies—rather than traditional metrics to justify interest rate cuts.
* **Policy Lag:** Booth argues the Fed is already "too late" to the easing process, noting that payroll revisions show net job destruction in the second and third quarters of 2025.

## The $1.8 Trillion Private Credit & CRE Warning
* **Write-Downs to Zero:** Booth highlights that firms like Ares Capital are already writing down big investments from par to zero, signaling the end of a seven-year period of low due diligence.
* **Liquidity Run Risks:** The Financial Stability Board is investigating the 1.8 trillion-dollar private credit market as retail investors follow institutions into these illiquid assets.
    * **Redemption Requests:** High redemption requests from "skittish" retail investors could force a broader market sell-off if they cannot exit illiquid private credit positions.
* **Commercial Real Estate (CRE) Distress:** With 30-year Treasury yields tapping 5%, the relief regional banks expected from falling rates has vanished.
    * **Fire Sales:** Office properties are seeing 90% discounts and distressed sales are at a decade high, further tightening lending standards.

## The K-Shaped Economy and Labor Market Decay
* **The "Severance Cliff":** While jobless claims appear low (189,000), Booth notes that only one in four unemployed Americans are actually collecting benefits, with a 40% exhaustion rate.
    * **Underemployment:** The job market has shifted toward low-quality, temporary, and contractor roles designed to execute AI implementations that eventually replace permanent staff.
* **Consumer Exhaustion:** Subprime and near-prime borrowers are now spending 16% of their monthly income on debt payments.
    * **Discretionary Slump:** Personal savings have hit their lowest point since 2022, leading to record-low numbers of Americans planning summer road trips.
* **Housing Market Freeze:** Mortgage rates returning to 6.3% have frozen the market, but re-listings are rising as layoffs (at firms like Meta and Estée Lauder) force families to monetize their primary assets.

## Industrial Recession and Global Capital Shifts
* **Manufacturing Margin Squeeze:** US manufacturers are "panic buying" inventory to get ahead of higher input costs and energy crises, while simultaneously slashing labor costs to protect margins.
* **The "Industrial Recession":** Booth predicts a "cliff dive" in manufacturing this summer as companies struggle with weaker demand and higher carrying costs.
* **Institutional Pivot to Gold:** Crypto entities (like Tether) and central banks are stockpiling physical gold, signaling a breakdown in institutional trust in the US dollar amid fears of "socialist" fiscal policies and persistent double-digit inflation.

## Notable Quotes
> "We've gone from par to zero. So the cracks continue to emerge, the distress continues to become more apparent... there’s big trouble when you’ve had effectively a seven-year period of very low due diligence." — **Danielle DiMartino Booth**

> "The exhaustion rate is 40%. So we're not actually looking at data through a true prism... only one in four Americans who are unemployed are actually collecting benefits." — **Danielle DiMartino Booth**

> "If the Fed is forced to lower interest rates too late because of what Jamie Dimon is referencing—a potential liquidity event—there's just going to be less money for [retirees] to spend." — **Danielle DiMartino Booth**

> "We are seeing 90% discounts on office properties. Office distressed sales are at a decade high." — **Danielle DiMartino Booth**
